title: Why identical seeds differ
question: What decides the traits a living thing ends up with?
hook: Two seeds with the same genes can grow to very different heights.
idea: Traits are passed down through distinct units from parents, and the environment also shapes what grows.

beats.prompt: Two corn seeds are genetically identical. One is planted in a temperate climate, the other in an arid climate with little rain. What happens?

choices.label: Both reach the same height, since their genes match
choices.feedback: It tempts because identical genes sound like identical results, but the environment also matters.

choices.label: The arid one grows to about half the height of the other
The arid one grows taller, because it has to struggle
choices.feedback: It sounds like toughness would pay off, but a lack of water and nutrients holds a plant back.

choices.label: The arid one does not grow at all
choices.feedback: Too extreme: it still grows, only to a smaller height.

beats.explain: Genes set the average height the stalks could reach, but the lack of water and nutrients holds the arid one to half the height.

beats.prompt: Put these events in the order they happened
items: Mendel presents his pea plant paper in Brno
Morgan argues genes are on chromosomes
beats.explain: Mendel presented his paper in 1865, his work was rediscovered in 1900, Bateson coined the word in 1905, and Morgan made his argument in 1911.

beats.prompt: Match each scientist to the idea tied to them
pairs: Pea plants inherit traits through discrete units
Sex is a chromosomal factor determined by the male
beats.explain: Each one added a different piece, from units of inheritance to the word itself to where genes sit and how sex is set.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which one?
steps: A man trains for years and builds big arms.
His training changes the genes he carries.
He passes those changed genes to his child.
So his child is born with bigger arms.
beats.explain: Experiences of individuals do not affect the genes they pass to their children, so the training leaves the inherited genes unchanged.
